name: EU/EEA/Swiss Free Movement

qualifying_event.description: EU, EEA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) and Swiss citizens have a right to enter, live, and work in Austria without a residence permit, under EU free-movement law. A 'Registration Certificate' (Anmeldebescheinigung) is required if staying beyond 3 months, but this is a formality, not a discretionary permit.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Valid EU/EEA/Swiss passport or ID card; registration with the residence authority after 3 months (proof of employment, self-employment, sufficient means, or study, plus health insurance).

requirements.blocker_text: Only nationals of EU, EEA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway), or Switzerland qualify for free movement into Austria.
Beyond 3 months, registration requires proof of employment/self-employment, sufficient means and health insurance (if economically inactive), or student status.

sources.title: workinaustria.com (AMS/ABA-run official relocation portal) -- Right of residence for EU/EEA nationals in Austria: free movement, Registration Certificate requirement after 3 months, self-sufficiency conditions

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Austria). Same EU/EEA/EFTA free-movement structure modeled for Sweden, Bulgaria, Finland, Luxembourg, Iceland, and Belgium in this dataset. citizenship_after_months (120) mirrors at_naturalisation.json's standard 10-year track since EU/EEA residence does not shorten Austria's naturalisation clock under the sources reviewed.
